question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of people who moved between municipalities within Japan in August 2026 (Japanese and foreign residents combined), as first reported in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident Registration.

target.what: Number of people who moved between municipalities within Japan (domestic internal migration) during August 2026, as first reported in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident Registration. Counts are based on Basic Resident Regist
target.unit: persons (count of moves/people recorded as moving between municipalities)
target.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
target.cadence: monthly, with preliminary figures for the reference month typically released around 6-8 weeks after month-end; the August 2026 report would be published in late September or October 2026, after the information cutoff
target.caveats: The target period is completed relative to the 2026-08-29 cutoff, but the official August 2026 report is not yet published. The estimate must rely on prior-year August values, recent 2026 monthly values, and any partial signals. The definition counts moves recorded in the Basic Resident Registration

candidates.hypothesis: August internal migration totals follow a strong seasonal pattern, with August typically one of the highest months due to summer relocations. The August 2026 value can be estimated by applying the historical August-to-annual ratio or the August-to-recent-month ratio to known 2026 monthly data.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total internal migration counts (Japanese + foreign combined) from the Statistics Bureau's Report on Internal Migration for January 2023 through July 2026, with August values for 2023, 2024, and 2025. Minimum evidence: the August 2025 total and the most recent 2026 monthly totals (e.g., June or July 2026) to anchor the level.
search_hints: Statistics Bureau Japan internal migration monthly report 2025 August
住民基本台帳人口移動報告 2025年8月 転入 転出
Japan internal migration statistics 2026 monthly

candidates.hypothesis: Internal migration counts are related to the size of the resident population and to the number of moves per capita. If the total population and the historical migration rate per 1,000 population are known, the August 2026 count can be approximated by population × monthly move rate, adjusted for seasonality.
candidates.data_to_find: Japan total population (Japanese + foreign residents) as of 2026 or latest available, and historical annual or monthly internal migration counts to compute a move rate per 1,000 population. Minimum evidence: a recent population estimate and a recent annual internal migration total.

candidates.hypothesis: The total internal migration count is the sum of Japanese and foreign resident moves. Foreign resident moves can be estimated from foreign population size and foreign-specific mobility rates, then added to Japanese moves. This route helps validate the combined total and assess the foreign share.
candidates.data_to_find: Number of foreign residents in Japan (latest available, e.g., 2025 or 2026), and any data on internal migration of foreign residents (e.g., from the same Statistics Bureau report or immigration statistics). Minimum evidence: foreign population total and a foreign internal migration count for a recent month or year.

candidates.hypothesis: The number of household moves is a physical flow that drives internal migration counts. If the average number of persons per moving household is known, the migration count can be approximated by the number of household moves × average household size. Moving company activity or utility transfers could serve as a proxy.
candidates.data_to_find: Number of household moves in Japan (e.g., from moving company associations, utility connection/disconnection data, or postal forwarding requests) for August or recent months, and average household size among movers. Minimum evidence: a monthly household move count and an average persons-per-move ratio.

assessment.note: All from the same ifa-leading.com summary of the Statistics Bureau's 2025 annual Report on Internal Migration; they describe the same underlying measurement (inter-municipal movers 5,190,548 in 2025, down 0.3% from 2024) decomposed into inter-prefecture and intra-prefecture components. They are one source, not independent confirmations, but they are internally consistent and give the 2025 annual level and recent trend.

p17 states movers are just over 4% of Japan's total population, i.e. about 1 in 25 people moved across municipalities in 2025. This is consistent with p12's 5.19 million annual inter-municipal movers against a population near 123-124 million. Same source, so it is a consistency check rather than independent evidence.

p18 (in-migrants from abroad up 6.3% in 2025) comes from the same report and same source as p12-p17. It is a different flow (international in-migration, not internal inter-municipal moves) and therefore does not directly corroborate the internal-migration level, but it is consistent with a year of roughly flat-to-slightly-declining internal mobility alongside rising foreign entries.

All are Libero/hikkoshi-rakunavi moving-job counts for 2025. They are internally consistent (p9's ~36% March-April concentration, p10's ~5x March/December ratio, p11's ~2x November/January ratio all match the monthly values). They measure moving-company job postings, not Basic Resident Registration moves, so they are a same-direction seasonal analogue rather than a measurement of the target.

Individual and corporate moving jobs for August 2025 are separate series from the same source; together they show August is a high but not peak month for moving activity, with the March-April corporate peak dominating the annual total.

assumptions.name: August share of annual inter-municipal movers
assumptions.rationale: August is a high but not peak month for Japanese residential moves; the moving-company analogue (p1, p2) shows August near the upper-middle of the monthly distribution, and the annual total is dominated by the March-April corporate peak. A share of roughly 9-10% of the annual total is consistent with a summer relocation bump plus the September school-year start. The range is widened to reflect uncertainty in transferring a moving-company seasonal pattern to Basic Resident Registration counts.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert the 2025 annual inter-municipal mover level (p12) into an August figure; assumes the 2026 August seasonal share is similar to recent years and that no major shock (disaster, policy change) distorts the pattern.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published monthly breakdown showing August's share of the annual total outside roughly 8-11.5%, or evidence of a 2026 shock that materially shifts summer relocation timing.

With no evidence of a large 2026 shift before the cutoff, a factor near 1.0 with a modest range is appropriate; the range reflects possible continuation of the slight decline or a small rebound.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to the 2025 annual level to project the 2026 annual level before extracting August; assumes no major demographic or policy shock in 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published 2026 monthly or partial-year data showing a change outside roughly -3% to +3% versus 2025.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
